newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: General Motors sees record Asian sales.
newsitem.headline: General Motors sees record Asian sales.

text.p: Singapore-based General Motors Asian and Pacific Operations (Pte) Ltd said on Friday its vehicle sales in the region grew to 624,300 units in 1996 against 619,100 the previous year.
It said in a statement that the results included sales by GM's strategic partner Isuzu Motors Ltd of Japan, in which GM has a 37.5 percent stake.
The statement said GM's overall market share for the Asia-Pacific region was 4.8 percent in 1996. Total industry sales for the region reached 12.95 million new vehicles.
Sales of GM passenger cars in 1996 declined 4.7 percent to 192,000 units.
The company attributed this to difficult market conditions in Taiwan and Thailand, where car sales were down 13 percent and seven percent, respectively.
In Japan, however, the GM group continued to dominate the imports market, becoming the leading importer for the second season in a row.
GM group commercial vehicle sales in 1996 numbered 432,300 units, up 3.5 percent over the previous year.
"Isuzu-produced vehicles accounted for most of those sales. In 1996, the commercial vehicle market in the region experienced a 1.3 percent decline in sales compared with 1995," it said.
